title: Setting goals before product-market fit: get users who love it, skip the graphs
summary: Dalton and Michael argue pre-PMF startups should ignore growth graphs and weekly growth targets, and focus on a ladder of real users who love the product (1, 10, 50, 100). Gmail and Stripe show great products start slow and obsessively served. Building for investors instead of users is a trap.

principles.text: With zero or few users, skip the graphs. Get something that someone loves first.
principles.quote: Don't even worry about graphs and charts and weekly growth. Just get something that someone loves.

principles.text: Use a user-count ladder as your goal: 1 real user, then 10, 50, 100 who love it. Graduate to graphs at 100.
principles.quote: if you could get 100 users or customers that love you, that is an awesome goal, and that's when I would start to graduate to graphs.

principles.text: Growth is the result of doing many things right, not the cause of a working company. Don't doctor metrics to hit a target.
principles.quote: growing 7% week over week is a result of doing a lot of things right. Whereas they think it is the cause of the company working.

principles.text: Don't build a startup to convince investors. Your customer is the user, not the investor.
principles.quote: If you start thinking this way that your entire startup is a product made to convince investors, you will not win.

principles.text: Great products often start tiny: Gmail had under 100 users for months, Stripe took two years to launch publicly. Test your startup assumptions against your favorite companies' early stories.
principles.quote: It was invite-only, it was beta-only. They built it for themselves for a side product and they only added customers super slow.

principles.text: Quantify the benefit customers get (like dollars earned), not just time spent. Early customer closeness, like Stripe's founders messaging customers daily, builds loyalty.
principles.quote: can you quantify the actual benefit of the customer as opposed to just time with you or that kind of stuff.
